name: Bar Wrist Curl
variant: Seated wrist flexion with a straight or EZ bar held palms-up while the forearms are supported on the thighs or a bench.
description: Sit with the forearms supported and palms facing up while holding a light bar, let the wrists extend under control without losing the grip, curl the bar upward by flexing the wrists, pause briefly, then lower through the same path without letting the elbows or shoulders move the load.

hypertrophy.rationale: Direct local forearm-flexor loading can build small target muscles, but the trained muscle mass and total overload ceiling are limited.

strength.rationale: Improves wrist-flexion force but does not express broad upper-body strength.

joint_resilience.rationale: Can provide controlled wrist-flexor and medial-elbow tendon exposure, but the signal is narrow and tolerance-sensitive.

athletic_transfer.rationale: Some grip and wrist-control relevance, but the seated isolated path has limited direct transfer.

control.rationale: Very low coordination demand beyond isolating the wrist and keeping the forearm still.

fatigue_efficiency.rationale: High local stimulus per systemic fatigue cost, though wrist and elbow irritation can limit useful hard sets.

setup.rationale: Requires only a light bar and a support surface, with little adjustment.

ease.rationale: The movement is easy to understand, but load selection and range control matter for wrist comfort.

progression.rationale: Reps and load are measurable, but useful jumps are small and many bars or plates progress too coarsely for wrist flexors.

support.rationale: The forearms are supported, and the movement can be isolated with minimal balance or trunk demand.

primary.name: Wrist flexors
primary.evidenceShort: Wrist flexion EMG directly measures flexor carpi activity.
primary.evidence: Wrist flexion and forearm-rotation EMG studies measured flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris during wrist-flexion output, supporting the wrist-flexor group as the visible primary target.

evidence.verdict: Bar wrist curl: wrist flexor group primary; no visible secondary or support muscles added.
evidence.clinicalShort: Surface EMG estimates acute excitation and coordination, not hypertrophy, pain response, or tendon safety.
evidence.limitsShort: Forearm support, wrist range, bar shape, load, tempo, grip, pronation/supination angle, and elbow position can change wrist-flexor demand.
evidence.summary: The bar wrist curl is classified as a supported wrist-flexion isolation exercise. Direct wrist-flexion EMG and forearm-rotation evidence support flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris, and related anterior-forearm muscles as the primary local targets. The app displays these as the aggregate Wrist flexors mesh group.
evidence.clinicalInterpretation: This movement is a small-muscle accessory. It can be useful for direct forearm loading, but performance should not be interpreted as a broad arm-strength measure.
evidence.limitations: The visible anatomy uses an aggregate forearm-flexor mesh group rather than separate FCR, FCU, FDS, FDP, and palmaris entries. Behind-the-back wrist curls, dumbbell wrist curls, cable wrist curls, wrist roller work, and finger curls should be separate variants if added.

studies.type: Forearm rotation and wrist muscle EMG
studies.shortCitation: Ikeda et al., J Orthop Surg Res, 2025
studies.finding: Wrist flexion output showed forearm-position-sensitive activity of flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris.
studies.citation: Ikeda K, Kaneoka K, Matsunaga N, Ikumi A, Yamazaki M, Yoshii Y. Effects of forearm rotation on wrist flexor and extensor muscle activities. Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research. 2025;20(1):53. doi:10.1186/s13018-024-05363-x.
studies.relevance: Direct wrist-flexion and wrist-extension EMG source for flexor and extensor role boundaries.

studies.finding: Dynamic wrist flexion-extension movement was used to characterize forearm muscle activity in young adults.
studies.citation: Forman DA, Forman GN, Avila-Mireles EJ, Mugnosso M, Zenzeri J, Murphy B, Holmes MWR. Characterizing forearm muscle activity in young adults during dynamic wrist flexion-extension movement using a wrist robot. Journal of Biomechanics. 2020;109908. doi:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2020.109908.
studies.relevance: Dynamic wrist movement EMG evidence for the local forearm-muscle classification.

studies.type: Forearm EMG during wrist and finger movements
studies.finding: Multi-channel EMG quantified forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movement tasks.
studies.citation: Gazzoni M, Celadon N, Mastrapasqua D, Paleari M, Margaria V, Ariano P. Quantifying forearm muscle activity during wrist and finger movements by means of multi-channel electromyography. PLoS ONE. 2014;9(10):e109943. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0109943.
studies.relevance: Broader forearm EMG source supporting wrist/finger movement muscle-group interpretation.
